title: Can you imagine playing a game that looks like this!
author: tomeks

comments.author: tomeks
comments.body:
used sora to bring this isometric image to life that I've generated in the past, used this prompt in sora:  
animate this isometric fantasy world, dynamic and alive, no transitions, no zoom, no camera movement  
see my previous creations at:  
[https://x.com/GigaPixelWorlds](https://x.com/GigaPixelWorlds)  
my next step is to gamify my obsession with isometric AI worlds :)

comments.author: CapoFerro
comments.body: The problem with most AI output is that it's all vibes and no specifics or nuance and certainly no gameplay. Sure the vibes are great but that's only a small piece of the puzzle. This is fine for a mood board.

replies.author: COMINGINH0TTT
replies.body: yeah but getting the right vibe is often the hardest part. The other things you mentioned are easier to develop imo

replies.author: CapoFerro
replies.body: I've been in the video game industry for many (many) years. I can't disagree more.

comments.author: adrixshadow
comments.body:
No. I prefer actual substance over form.

What does all those buildings mean, what is their function, what is their purpose?

It means nothing, it's all set dressing.
